h: פָּרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים, מַאֲמָר י״א Parshas Shekalim — Maamar Yud Aleph

p: and in the Pesikta Rabbasi (parshah 10, siman 1):
Why do they begin in Adar
and take up the terumah from Nissan?
So as not to press Yisrael;
is a small matter in our times,
וְלִכְאוֹרָה מַה שַּׁיְּיךְ עַל זֶה הַטַּעַם
and seemingly how does the reason apply to it,
regarding the measure of a perutah,
that it is a small matter,
yet it is money to betroth a woman and the like;
and he answered that even though in our times
there are the wealthy of the people,
and it is a small matter;
as it says in Nechemiah chapter 5,
a perutah was then something significant;
And this is what they said,
שֶׁהָיוּ מַזְהִירִין אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל מֵרֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ
that they would remind Yisrael from Rosh Chodesh:
this is what we learn in Shekalim
that is, by proclamation of the Beis Din,
and it was not on Shabbos
was that each one of Yisrael prepare his shekel
in order to take up the terumah on Rosh Chodesh Nissan
and they began early, from Rosh Chodesh Adar,
so as not to press Yisrael.
But the reading of Parshas Shekalim
or on Rosh Chodesh when it falls on Shabbos —
it is impossible to say that it is to announce,
since they proclaim from Rosh Chodesh;
דְּקָאָמַר כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלֵיתוּ שְׁקָלִים וְכוּלֵּי
which says, "so that the shekalim will come," etc.,
it is evident that the enactment of reading Parshas Shekalim
existed in the time of the Beis HaMikdash as well.
And likewise according to Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
it answers that it is because of the money-changers' tables;
The matter: it states in the Yotzer for this parshah
(at the end of the piece beginning "Omen"):
"Merciful One, as You had mercy on Your espoused
And likewise in Mussaf (the piyut of the Modim blessing):
"May the pure speech of our lips
for there is no silver of the shekels of atonement."
"let our lips take the place of bulls"
וּמַה שַּׁיְּיכוּת שִׁלּוּם פָּרִים עַל שְׁקָלִים
so what connection has "in place of bulls" with shekalim?
But the reading of Parshas Shekalim
שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם קוֹדֶם רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן
thirty days before Rosh Chodesh Nissan
is to make a preparation for the shekalim,
from which they would offer the korbanos,
וְעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג ז, ב)
and about this they said (Zohar III 7b):
Yisrael sustain their Father in Heaven;
רַק עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל תָּרְמוּ שִׁקְלֵיהֶן.
except through Yisrael contributing their shekels.
And Yisrael needed a preparation for this
שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם קוֹדֶם רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן
thirty days before Rosh Chodesh Nissan,
when they took up the new terumah;
and the preparation was through reading the parshah,
and it had to be specifically on Shabbos,
דְּאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
as it states in the holy Zohar (II 88a):
וְהַאי יוֹמָא מַלְיָא רֵישֵׁיהּ דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין
"and on this day the head of Ze'eir Anpin is filled
with the dew that descends from the holy Atika," etc.;
that is, through the three meals,
which are in the secret of "oneg":
ע׳ עֵדֶן נ׳ נָהָר ג׳ גַּן
ayin, Eden; nun, river; gimmel, garden,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א כו, א)
as they said in the Zohar (I 26a);
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַלְיָא רֵישֵׁיהּ דִּזְעֵיר אַנְפִּין
and through this the head of Ze'eir Anpin is filled
with the dew of the holy Atika;
that Yisrael sustain, as it were,
are called the meals of the King
like the korbanos, "My bread for My fire-offerings";
הוּא גַּם כֵּן טַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
is also the dew of Torah she'b'al peh,
as has been explained many times
from the holy Zohar and the Tikkunei Zohar
And Yisrael needed to make the preparation on Shabbos,
even for one who contributed his shekel
on the eve of Rosh Chodesh Nissan.
And on the fifteenth of Adar
the tables were set up in the provinces,
so that whoever had it in hand
would perform the act of the mitzvah
שְׁתֵּי שַׁבָּתוֹת קוֹדֶם רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ נִיסָן
two weeks before Rosh Chodesh Nissan;
and all this was a preparation
so that each one of Yisrael would be able
who sustain their Father in Heaven.
that they should prepare the shekels,
and so as not to press Yisrael,
And this is what they said in the Pesikta (ibid., siman 11):
and the head of Yisrael is none other
than the Holy One, blessed be He,
as it says (Michah 2:13), "and Hashem at their head";
and it gives several parables about this;
And this is the intent of what they said,
the head of Ze'eir Anpin will be filled
with the dew that descends from the holy Atika;
and this is what it says, "Ki sisa
which is the Holy One, blessed be He.
עַל יְדֵי פָּרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים בִּזְמַן הַבַּיִת.
through Parshas Shekalim in the time of the Beis HaMikdash.
And this is what the paytan says
when we have neither korbanos nor shekalim:
"so turn to our lips in place of offering bulls,"
and likewise, "the pure speech of our lips
for although the act of the mitzvah is lacking,
that it be "My bread for My fire-offerings,"
"let our lips take the place of bulls":
that the reading of Parshas Shekalim
will count like the act of the shekalim
and be a preparation for the whole year,
that the reading of the verses of the korbanos
be as though they offer bulls, the bread of Hashem,
and all Yisrael will sustain, as it were,
their Father in Heaven, as mentioned above.
that Yisrael eat in honor of Shabbos
are called the meals of the King,
for the head of Ze'eir Anpin is filled
with the dew that descends from the holy Atika
and drips down to the Field of Apples,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם [פח, א]
as they said in the holy Zohar there (88a):
in the holy Atika, in Ze'eir Anpin,
and in the Field of Apples, etc.
are called the meals of faith, etc.,
complete faith in all its aspects,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם עַמּוּד ב)
as they said in the holy Zohar (there, side b);
that is, the three Shabbos meals
correspond to the three holinesses mentioned,
which are complete faith, as mentioned above;
and therefore they too are called
the meals of the King, like the korbanos.

paragraphs.text: Tanchuma, Ki Sisa 1; Pesikta Rabbati 10:1 — “They would begin collecting from the first of Adar, and take the contribution on the first of Nisan. Why do they begin in Adar and take it in Nisan? So as not to press Israel. They would warn Israel from the first of the month.” Pesikta Rabbati 10:1 gives the same explanation and states that the funds purchased the daily offerings so all Israel would be partners in them. The warning in Adar allows time to prepare the contribution.

paragraphs.text: Responsa Rivash 153 — “You assessed the people of Majorca, whose wealthy had houses full of every good thing, stores of silver and merchandise, pearls and gold. But assess the inhabitants of this land, who lack even scant bread and measured water, sleep on the ground or a skin mat, cover themselves at night in their daytime clothing, wear patch upon patch, and mostly go barefoot. In the Sages’ time it was so. The Men of the Great Assembly, when they returned from exile, were exceedingly poor, as the account of Nechemiah records. Consider: a woman is betrothed with a perutah, though it is a very small thing; and a court hears a claim for a perutah, since it is not presumed forgiven.” The responsum answers an objection to the small monetary value of the statutory kesubah. It bases the standard on the poor and concludes that those who wish may add. Rav Tzadok applies this historical measure of value to the advance notice for the half shekel.

paragraphs.text: Shekalim piyyutim: Omen and Mussaf Modim — “Merciful One, as You had mercy upon those borne by You through the silver of atonement, so regard our lips as repayment in bulls. ‘May the pure utterance of our lips repay bulls, for the silver of the atoning shekels is no more.’” The first passage closes Omen in the Shekalim morning liturgy; the second appears in the Modim insertion of the Mussaf piyyut, beginning Ein otzem. Both adapt Hoshea’s “we shall repay bulls with our lips” to the loss of the shekel offering. The digital liturgical witnesses read beshillum parim, “as repayment in bulls.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 7b — “When sustenance is found below, sustenance is found above. It is like a king who prepared his own feast but had not prepared food for his servants. When he prepared for his servants, he ate his meal and they ate theirs. ‘I ate my honeycomb with my honey’—this is the King’s meal. ‘Eat, friends; drink and become intoxicated, beloved ones’—this is their meal from the fragrance of the offering when its fragrance ascended. Therefore the King’s meal waited for the servants’ meal. For this reason we learned that Israel sustain their Father in Heaven. Who eats of the King’s meal? The souls of the righteous.” The source speaks through a royal parable of sacrifice and reciprocal nourishment. Rav Tzadok extends that sacrificial preparation to the shekel funds and then to Shabbos meals.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 88a — “Rabbi Abba said: Blessing is prepared for those supernal days, which are blessed from this day. On this day the head of Zeir Anpin is filled with dew descending from Atika Kadisha, the most concealed of all. He pours it upon the field of holy apples three times from the entrance of Shabbos, so that all will be blessed together.” The threefold flow of dew is the specific basis for linking the three Shabbos meals to the upper and lower modes of receiving blessing.

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 26a — “At that time it was said of Moshe and Israel: ‘Then you will delight in Hashem’—with oneg, whose letters signify ayin: Eden; nun: river; gimel: garden. The verse ‘Then Moshe will sing’ will be fulfilled: it does not say he sang, but he will sing. For the mixed multitude oneg becomes nega, affliction; but for Israel there will be delight.” The interpretation treats oneg as the connected sequence Eden–river–garden, through which delight is communicated. Rav Tzadok reads the meals through that ordered flow.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sod Yesharim, Yom Kippur 17 — “The divine will set in creation that every soul be nourished by things lower than itself, so that a person raise all things to their root; this is ‘Yisrael sustain their Father in Heaven,’ for by raising the lower things he makes a pleasing aroma to Hashem.” The Radziner explains how eating, like an offering, can “sustain” above, the basis for calling the Shabbos meals the King’s meals.

paragraphs.text: Mishnah Shekalim 1:3 — “On the fifteenth, money changers would sit in the provinces. On the twenty-fifth they sat in the Temple. Once they sat in the Temple, they began taking pledges.” This is the collection schedule behind the maamar’s distinction between preparation through reading, the later opportunity to perform the monetary mitzvah, and the original announcement.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Sefas Emes, Pekudei–Shekalim 5643 (1883), final paragraph — “‘They announce in Adar and collect in Nisan.’ They gave a month for preparation of the gift, because the purpose is not the shekel, but the desire and generosity of the heart. Therefore preparation for the mitzvah is more beloved than its principal act; this is the joy of a mitzvah. The surplus in Israel’s donation alludes to this, showing that the generosity and desire rise beyond the act itself. But the taxes and levies of the wicked, whose purpose is only money, are called ‘the path of the lazy.’”

paragraphs.text: Connection: This passage addresses the same month between announcement and collection, interpreting it as time for the heart’s preparation. It sharpens Rav Tzadok’s distinction between the court’s practical announcement and the Shabbos reading’s preparation for participation in the communal offerings.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Radak on Hoshea 14:3 — “In place of bulls we will pay before You the confession of our lips, for You desire words of teshuvah more; the offerings avail nothing without confession of the sin.” Radak shows that words were always the inner core of the offering, which grounds the piyut’s plea that our reading of Parshas Shekalim be accepted as the shekalim themselves.

paragraphs.text: Zohar II, 88a–b — “A person must delight at these three times, for the supernal faith depends on them: Atika Kadisha, Zeir Anpin, and the field of apples. He must delight and rejoice in them. Rabbi Abba would rejoice in each Shabbos meal and say: ‘This is the holy meal of Atika Kadisha, the most concealed of all.’ At another meal he would say: ‘This is the meal of the Holy One, blessed be He.’ When he finished the meals he said: ‘The meals of faith have been completed.’ When Rabbi Shimon came to a meal he would say: ‘Prepare the meal of supernal faith; prepare the King’s meal,’ and would sit and rejoice.” The passage calls the meals both the King’s meal and meals of faith. The first description concerns the divine recipient and flow of blessing; the second concerns the complete threefold pattern in which the person participates.
